I am auditing an effort estimate for a ticket about "PDP – Maximum Purchase Quantity Override by Customer Group and SKU". I need precise, evidence-led facts with absolute file paths and line numbers. Search VERY THOROUGHLY.

Answer these questions:

1. **Find the current max-quantity cap.** A prior investigation claims the current 3-per-SKU purchase cap is a HARDCODED CONSTANT in the PDP code, not a Salesforce-backed field. Confirm or refute. Grep across `overrides/` for: `MAX_ORDER_QUANTITY`, `maxOrderQuantity`, `max_order_quantity`, `MAX_QUANTITY`, `maxQuantity`, `quantityLimit`, `MAX_`, `stepQuantity`, `numberOfItems`, and any literal `3` used as a quantity cap. Look especially in:
   - `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/`
   - `overrides/app/components/product-detail-options/` (or similar)
   - `overrides/app/components/quantity-picker/` or `zimmQuantity*`
   - `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/` (atoms/molecules/organisms)
   Report the EXACT file path, line number, and the literal code for any cap you find.

2. **Compare with base SFCC.** Grep `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/` for the same terms. What does base SFCC do for max order quantity out of the box? Does the base `product-view` / `quantity-picker` read anything from the product object (e.g. `product.inventory.stockLevel`, `stepQuantity`, `minOrderQuantity`)? Report file paths.

3. **Where is quantity enforced?** Trace the add-to-cart / add-to-bag path on PDP. Which component owns the quantity state, which validates it, and where does the "limit reached" message (if any) render? Report file paths + the message text/i18n key if present.

4. **Overrides inventory.** Which of these exist as overrides already (i.e. the copy-first cost is already paid) vs only in node_modules? List each with its absolute path: `product-detail` page, `product-view`, `product-detail-options`, `quantity-picker`, `swatch-group`, `product-item`, `add-to-cart-modal`.

5. **Customer-group awareness.** Is there ANY client-side customer-group logic anywhere in `overrides/`? Grep for `customerGroup`, `customer_group`, `customerGroups`, `groupIds`, `usid`, and check what `useCurrentCustomer` / `overrides/app/hooks/use-current-customer.ts` actually returns — does the customer object expose customer group membership at all? Check `node_modules/commerce-sdk-isomorphic/dist/` types for `ShopperCustomers` customer shape re: groups. This is central to the estimate.

Be exhaustive on #1 and #5. Report file paths absolutely. Do not write any files.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'inspect' returns the accessibility tree of the front app (what a screen reader reads, which can differ from what is drawn) as JSON — per element: type, label, value, frame [x,y,width,height] in device points from the top-left, traits the type does not imply, enabled only when false, children. Call 'inspect' before a 'tap' on anything you have not located in this screen's tree, before answering what text a screen shows, and before reporting a control's state (a switch's value, whether a button is enabled, which tab is selected) or whether a sheet, alert or other modal is in front (the result says so) — never guess coordinates from memory of similar apps, and do not 'screenshot' for these. Go straight to 'screenshot' for color, images, and layout. Three reads: no marker and no x/y = the whole visible tree (the safe default when you do not know the exact label); marker = the first element, in tree order, whose label contains that CASE-SENSITIVE substring — a title can match before the button with the same text, so check the matched element's type; x/y = the element drawn on top at that point, as a tap would find it, with its descendants (a point between controls hits their container). If a marker misses or returns the wrong element, read the whole tree instead of guessing or screenshotting. Then tap the center of the target's frame. Hidden, off-screen, and illegibly small elements are omitted and counted; text longer than its area shows is cut (it ends with ...). Only the x/y read resolves occlusion, and only by bars and containers it can recognize: a frame from the whole-tree or marker read that overlaps a later sibling (a tab bar, a sheet) may be covered, so before tapping it read x/y at its center; a point on a sheet's blank area can still read the content behind it, so when the result reports a modal, stay inside it. A tree over the size cap loses its deepest levels first and says so — narrow with marker, or with x/y on the target itself: a point in a gap answers the container around it, which is no smaller; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the currently attached simulator, or the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

Omit for the whole tree (the safe default), or pass x/y instead for the element under a point.

1	import type { ShopperProductsTypes } from 'commerce-sdk-isomorphic';
2	
3	/**
4	 * `c_maxOrderQuantity` is a Zimmermann-custom SFCC attribute — a real BM site preference
5	 * (Integer, default 3, min 1, per-site) surfaced onto the SCAPI product response via a
6	 * `dw.ocapi.shop.product.afterGET` hook, per Confluence `TSD-SFCC-268` (406913046). It has no
7	 * typed field on the base SDK's `Product` type — it only reaches this shape via that type's own
8	 * `{[key: string]: any}` index signature, the same situation
9	 * `overrides/app/pages/product-list/productListCardMapper.ts` lines 16-23 document for a
10	 * different custom attribute (`c_productBadges`). Narrowed here to a local type rather than
11	 * trusting `any` at the call site, per AGENTS.md's Gotchas: "Commerce SDK types not importable
12	 * ... declare a narrow local type."
13	 *
14	 * Typed `unknown`, not `number | undefined`: this function's whole job is validating a value
15	 * that may legitimately arrive absent, as `0`, negative, or non-numeric (see the pass criteria
16	 * this file's own test covers) — typing it as `number | undefined` would assert a guarantee the
17	 * real BM data doesn't have.
18	 *
19	 * As of this commit `TSD-SFCC-268` is still `v0.1 Draft` (Technical Lead sign-off Pending) and a
20	 * live dev-sandbox probe found no `c_maxOrderQuantity` on any product — the `afterGET` hook is
21	 * not deployed yet. Reading the field with the fallback below degrades to today's hardcoded
22	 * behaviour while that remains true, and picks up the real per-site value the day the hook ships,
23	 * with no further frontend change needed.
24	 */
25	type ProductWithMaxOrderQuantity = ShopperProductsTypes.Product & {
26	  c_maxOrderQuantity?: unknown;
27	};
28	
29	/**
30	 * Frontend fallback when no valid `c_maxOrderQuantity` is present. Matches
31	 * `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx`'s own `MAX_PURCHASE_QUANTITY` value (3) exactly
32	 * (see that file's lines 124-125: "Frontend-enforced limit (SFCC-196). SFCC has no platform
33	 * max-order-quantity field."), but is deliberately its own, independent constant rather than a
34	 * shared/promoted one — the TSD's resolution order is product override (SFCC-703) -> site
35	 * preference -> this hardcoded value, so a constant shared between the PDP and this cart-facing
36	 * util would need reworking the day the real per-site preference ships anyway.
37	 */
38	const DEFAULT_MAX_ORDER_QUANTITY = 3;
39	
40	/**
41	 * Reads the real per-product order-quantity cap off a SCAPI product response
42	 * (`c_maxOrderQuantity`), falling back to `DEFAULT_MAX_ORDER_QUANTITY` when the attribute is
43	 * absent or not a valid, usable cap (zero, negative, or non-numeric) — see this file's own
44	 * module docblock for why a shared constant is deliberately not used here.
45	 *
46	 * @param product A SCAPI product response (or product-shaped object) that may carry
47	 * `c_maxOrderQuantity`.
48	 * @returns The product's real max order quantity, or `DEFAULT_MAX_ORDER_QUANTITY` (3) when no
49	 * valid value is present.
50	 */
51	export const getMaxOrderQuantity = (product: ProductWithMaxOrderQuantity): number => {
52	  const value = product?.c_maxOrderQuantity;
53	  return typeof value === 'number' && Number.isFinite(value) && value > 0 ? value : DEFAULT_MAX_ORDER_QUANTITY;
54	};

I have everything. Here are the evidence-led findings.

---

## 1. The current max-quantity cap — the prior investigation is PARTIALLY WRONG

There are **two independent caps**, not one, and only the PDP one is purely hardcoded.

### A. PDP cap — HARDCODED. Claim CONFIRMED for the PDP.

`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx`

```
148: /** Frontend-enforced limit (SFCC-196). SFCC has no platform max-order-quantity field. */
149: const MAX_PURCHASE_QUANTITY = 3;
```

Consumed at exactly one place, line 1330-1331:
```
1330:                  maxOrderQuantity={MAX_PURCHASE_QUANTITY}
1331:                  basketProductItems={basket?.productItems ?? []}
```

Module-scope `const`, no export, no config, no Salesforce read. This is the only cap on the PDP.

### B. Cart cap — already Salesforce-backed (with a hardcoded fallback). Claim REFUTED for the cart.

`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/utils/maxOrderQuantity.ts`

```
38: const DEFAULT_MAX_ORDER_QUANTITY = 3;
...
51: export const getMaxOrderQuantity = (product: ProductWithMaxOrderQuantity): number => {
52:   const value = product?.c_maxOrderQuantity;
53:   return typeof value === 'number' && Number.isFinite(value) && value > 0 ? value : DEFAULT_MAX_ORDER_QUANTITY;
54: };
```

This is materially important to your estimate. The file's own docblock (lines 3-36) documents that:
- `c_maxOrderQuantity` is a **Zimmermann-custom SFCC attribute** — a real BM site preference (Integer, default 3, min 1, per-site) surfaced onto SCAPI via a `dw.ocapi.shop.product.afterGET` hook, per Confluence `TSD-SFCC-268` (page id 406913046).
- As of that commit, TSD-SFCC-268 was **still v0.1 Draft, Technical Lead sign-off Pending**, and a live dev-sandbox probe found **no `c_maxOrderQuantity` on any product — the afterGET hook is not deployed**.
- The TSD's stated resolution order is: **product override (SFCC-703) → site preference → hardcoded value**. Note: that resolution order is per-product/per-site — **customer group is not in it.**
- Lines 31-36 explicitly state the duplication is deliberate: `DEFAULT_MAX_ORDER_QUANTITY` is independent of the PDP's `MAX_PURCHASE_QUANTITY` rather than shared, because a shared constant "would need reworking the day the real per-site preference ships anyway."

Consumers of `getMaxOrderQuantity` (all cart-side, none on PDP):
- `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/product-item/index.tsx:168` (import), `:363` — `max={getMaxOrderQuantity(product)}`
- `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/hooks/useCartMergeAndCap.ts:4`, `:43-44`

### Implication for the estimate
Nothing in the frontend knows, or can cheaply learn, which customer group the shopper is in. The three plausible routes all carry server-side dependency:

1. **Extend the existing `c_maxOrderQuantity` hook** to resolve group server-side and emit an already-group-resolved number per SKU. Cheapest frontend (the util and its four call sites already exist), but it depends on TSD-SFCC-268's `afterGET` hook, which per `maxOrderQuantity.ts:19-23` **is still v0.1 Draft, unsigned-off, and not deployed to the dev sandbox**. The frontend currently only ever exercises the fallback-of-3 path — confirmed by the test at `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/product-item/index.test.tsx:478-481` and the story comment at `index.stories.tsx:238-239`.
2. **Add a `c_customerGroups` custom attribute** to the customer response and resolve the cap client-side. Requires the same class of SFCC server work, plus new frontend group-matching logic that does not exist anywhere today.
3. **Shopper Context `customerGroupIds`** — will not work as a read path (write-only qualifier), and the cache-invalidation side effect is a real cost.

Also note TSD-SFCC-268's documented resolution order (`maxOrderQuantity.ts:34-35`) is **product override → site preference → hardcoded** — customer group is **not** a tier in the already-specified design, so this ticket expands the agreed TSD, it does not just implement it.
